title: The Brazilian Churrasco Board
seo_title: Brazilian Churrasco Board: Picanha, Coalho & Chimichurri
description: A Brazilian churrasco board with grilled picanha, linguiça, queijo coalho, pão de queijo, grilled pineapple and farofa. What to buy for 8–10.
hook: A steakhouse-style spread built around grilled picanha and squeaky grilled cheese. It needs a grill, but everything else comes together in half an hour.
why: Churrasco is about beef and fire, so picanha sits at the center with its fat cap grilled crisp, joined by garlicky linguiça and salty carne seca. Queijo coalho is a firm cheese made for the grill: it browns and softens without melting, and pão de queijo and creamy requeijão give the cheese side two softer textures.

Everything else is there to cut the richness. Chimichurri and molho à campanha bring vinegar and fresh herbs, grilled pineapple adds sweet-tart juice (a churrascaria classic), and passion fruit and lime keep things bright. Farofa, cassava chips and Brazil nuts add crunch.

timeline.what: Grill the picanha and linguiça, rest 5 minutes, then slice thin.
Grill the coalho and pineapple slices.
Make the chimichurri and warm the garlic bread.
Arrange the meats and cheeses on the board.
Add the sauces, farofa and fruit; garnish with cilantro and lime.

faq.q: Where can I buy picanha and queijo coalho?
faq.a: Ask a butcher for top sirloin cap with the fat left on; some call it coulotte or rump cap. Queijo coalho and requeijão are sold at Brazilian and Latin markets and online. Halloumi is the easiest stand-in for coalho.
Toasted manioc (cassava) flour, often cooked in butter with onion or bacon. Brazilians sprinkle it over grilled meat for crunch. Buttered toasted breadcrumbs work in a pinch.

faq.q: What should I drink with a churrasco board?
faq.a: A caipirinha, made with cachaça, lime and sugar, is the classic. For wine, a juicy red like Malbec stands up to the grilled beef.
Make the chimichurri and vinaigrette a day ahead and chill them. Grill the meat and cheese just before serving; coalho firms up as it cools, so serve it warm.
